text: Umbilical cord: soak in iodine as soon as possible after birth to prevent microbes entering; cutting and tying off the cord after disinfecting is better since it can otherwise bleed. Teeth clipping: prevents fighting injuries between piglets and damage to the sow's teats during nursing; must be done before 3 days of age, taking care not to damage the gums. Tail docking: reduces tail-biting and related infection as pigs get older — cut half to three-quarters of the tail quickly, disinfect both the tail and the scalpel with iodine, and complete this before 3 days of age.
